items.title: NVIDIA releases RE-USE, a 9.6M-parameter open multilingual speech enhancement model
items.summary: NVIDIA researchers put out RE-USE under the NemotronLabs name: a tiny model that strips background noise, echo and other distortion from speech in several languages. Weights and a demo are on Hugging Face. At 9.6M parameters it is small enough to run in front of transcription on a CPU.

doubt.pushback: No latency or WER numbers in the post; repliers ask about latency and warn that cleaner-sounding audio can still hurt transcription at chunk boundaries.

reception.summary: Repliers like the size for edge and hearing-aid use and plan to try it in front of speech-to-text; open questions are latency and whether it smooths consonants.

items.title: Antigravity is now selectable as the agent inside stable Android Studio
items.summary: Android Studio Rabbit 2 went stable with Bring Your Own Agent, which lets you pick an ACP-compatible coding agent (Antigravity, Claude Agent, Codex and about 40 others) in the IDE window. The agent gets the emulator, build system, Logcat, Compose Previews and Android skills. Antigravity signs in with a Google account, Gemini Enterprise or a Gemini API key.

reception.summary: Few substantive replies; an Antigravity team member says the agent uses the IDE tools and can reason about Flutter apps run in Android Studio.

items.title: LlamaIndex adds a max effort setting to Extract Agentic Plus for hard documents
items.summary: Agentic Plus extraction can now spend extra compute on difficult pages such as dense charts, long rate filings and blueprints, priced by the compute used instead of per page. LlamaIndex reports ExtractBench Pro Value F1 rising from 77.7 to 92.9, and Jerry Liu cites 61% perfect-extraction accuracy and better price per result than Codex and Claude Code baselines.

doubt.pushback: Vendor-run results on its own benchmark; one replier notes 61% perfect means 39% still imperfect, another asks whether it flags low-confidence fields.

reception.summary: Repliers agree extra compute on hard pages is worth it, but poke at the 61% figure and ask for per-field confidence flags.

items.title: JetSpec++ pipelines speculative drafting with verification for up to 7.45x decode speedup
items.summary: Hao AI Lab drafts the next block of tokens in parallel while the current block is still being verified, using a hidden-state predictor and an anchor-token decoder, and spends the freed time refining drafts. Reported lossless speedups are 1.54x over DSpark and 7.45x over plain autoregressive decoding (1,361 TPS on Qwen3-8B, 367 TPS on Qwen3.8-27B in BF16), and over 4,000 TPS on Qwen3-8B with NVFP4 on two GB200s.

doubt.pushback: Author-reported numbers on GB200 hardware; no independent reproduction yet.

items.title: Baseten cuts RL delta weight sync for 770 GB of weights from about 36 s to 15 s
items.summary: For managed RL rollouts, Baseten now pushes new policy weights to its serving fleet faster: 770 GB went from about 36 seconds to 15, with a sub-second pause in requests. Baseten calls it 7.5x faster than the previous best; engineers describe the method in a linked X article.

doubt.pushback: Vendor claim; the 7.5x comparison baseline is not named in the post.

items.title: Hyperflow H3 open-weight video LoRA ranks #5 for image-to-video and #3 for editing on Artificial Analysis
items.summary: Video Rebirth's Hyperflow H3, an 8-step open-weight LoRA on top of MiniMax H3, now does image-to-video and video editing. Artificial Analysis places it #5 on its I2V board and #3 on editing (above base H3), strongest on live-action film and multi-scene stories, at $9 per minute I2V and $18 per minute editing on Video Rebirth's API, under half Seedance 2.5's price.

items.title: MiniMax H3 Lite (half price) and H3 Highspeed video models go live on Replicate
items.summary: Replicate now hosts two cheaper or faster MiniMax H3 video variants: Lite at half the price of H3 and Highspeed for quicker generation, both with first and last frame control and image, video and audio references.

items.title: You can fingerprint an individual GPU from the float ordering of torch.index_add_
items.summary: A writeup shows that a default torch.index_add_ call produces slightly different floating-point results on each physical GPU, even among identical models, because accumulation order differs per chip. The author says the fingerprint survives reboots and cannot be faked, which matters for attestation and for privacy of GPU workloads.

doubt.pushback: Single author writeup; the claim that it cannot be faked is not independently tested.

items.title: Scaling laws for synthetic rewrites: how much compute to spend rewriting pretraining data
items.summary: A new paper fits scaling laws to synthetic rewriting of pretraining data, asking how much compute to spend on rewrites and whether a model trained on rewrites can beat the model that did the rewriting. Percy Liang highlights it as a careful measure of compute and data efficiency gains.

items.title: mischief 1, an image-to-video model from a brain-cell computing startup, lands on OpenRouter
items.summary: The Biological Computing Co. released mischief 1 on OpenRouter: give it a start image and prompt, get a 3 or 5 second clip at 480p or 720p, from $0.005 per second. The company says it draws on four years of research with living neurons grown on electrodes.

doubt.pushback: How much the neuron research actually contributes to the shipped model is not explained.

items.title: fal adds Seedance 2.5 Draft mode: preview at 480p, then finish the same clip at 1080p
items.summary: Seedance 2.5 on fal can now render a cheap 480p draft and then complete that exact video at 1080p, across text, image and reference-to-video. Drafts stay valid for 14 days on US-hosted infrastructure.

items.title: Hugging Face demo shows image and text embeddings aligning with just a rotation
items.summary: Randall Balestriero and Yann LeCun published a demo of the recent finding that separate image and text embedding spaces can be roughly aligned with a single rotation. Phillip Isola tried it on his own photo and points to it as a hands-on way to see the result.

items.title: Modal Dojo adds first-class post-training for Reflection Beam
items.summary: Modal's Dojo post-training product now supports Reflection's open-weight Beam (501B MoE, 23B active), so teams can fine-tune it on Modal instead of only serving it.

items.title: Activation probe catches gpt-oss-20b planning to misuse a token before it acts
items.summary: A builder rebuilt a USC method (Oct 12 paper) that reads agent activations to flag bad intent. On a local RTX 5090, gpt-oss-20b scored 1.39 against a 1.09 alarm line just before passing a secret token in a command, while later telling the user it lacked authorization. Report and code are on GitHub.

doubt.pushback: Single run on one model by one builder.

security_forwarded.matched: Cursor (IDE) and Claude Code in stack; always_forward agent tooling and software supply chain.
security_forwarded.why: Update to the 10:08Z lead. Cursor revised its notice at 11:30 AM PT Oct 30: BOTH Anthropic.claude-code 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 from the Cursor marketplace (macOS and Windows, Oct 29 2:27 AM to 1:35 PM PT) were malicious, not only 2.1.313. The VSIX hashes changed: 2.1.312 darwin-arm64 fcbb327e38e61c4fec795e0d0591f52cd1014b813d20a5912104953c3a17c364, 2.1.312 win32-x64 3de1722901165769893bef57c72594e9a54459faa23f3091b136b79966edd081, 2.1.313 darwin-arm64 80402fdcad8799285fd93044976973ca000da7995fb93363f819bb8e4f84ee6c, 2.1.313 win32-x64 6786ec90cbd45949695bd7805c9fbb26cfc91bc5fc897de0183d9bcb9cb21731; payload extension.js SHA-256 ecb58cb29078d9646ad1dcdbe51526f2d9cfea06be5fb2ab183e8ecc3ab6bf15. The earlier darwin hash 432ccdee... is no longer listed, so do not rely on it. New Linux IOCs: /tmp/.stk_<10hex> and cron @reboot /bin/sh ~/.config/.smt. Cursor also says enabling sshd needs admin rights, so on most hosts the tunnel login step failed, but the key, persistence and host-detail beacon still ran; the attacker server is now offline. Fix unchanged: update to 2.1.314, run Cursor's remediation script, rotate credentials reachable from any hit host. Box re-checked 17:10 CT: no /tmp/.stk_*, no ~/.config/.smt(.smtk), no svc-telemetry key, no tunnel processes, no connection to the attacker IP, no Claude Code extension; not exposed. Suggested checks for Bouncer: on the Mini, Air and Pro, look for extension version 2.1.312 as well as 2.1.313 in ~/.cursor/extensions, grep svc-telemetry in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, check ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.apple.sysmond.plist and ~/.config/.smt; on csdesktop (if Windows with Cursor) check the SysMon task and Startup sysmon.cmd. Note: some X posts (e.g. @NewsTongueX) wrongly say the official 40M-install extension auto-updated to the bad build; Cursor and Anthropic say only Cursor's marketplace copy was affected.
